Problem Statement:
Strip problematic private escape sequences

## Type of changes

- [x] Bug fix

- [ ] Other

## Checklist

- [x] I've run the latest [black](https://github.com/psf/black) with default args on new code.
- [x] I've updated CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTORS.md where appropriate.
- [x] I've added tests for new code.
- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

["Private escape sequences"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Fp_Escape_sequences) are escape sequences that are reserved for private use, though `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are commonly used for storing and restoring the current cursor position. When those escape codes are not stripped the cursor jumps around and causes Rich to write garbage output. An example of a program that uses this cursor store/restore functionality is the APK package manager in Alpine Linux:

https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/apk-tools/-/blob/48d91f482eb48a0a107b714ee183bb7e07782e14/src/print.c#L232-240

This commit updates the ANSI parser to ignore the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` escape sequences, thus preventing them from being printed and causing havoc.

)

    """Result of ansi tokenized string."""

    plain: str = ""
    sgr: Optional[str] = ""
    osc: Optional[str] = ""

    """Tokenize a string in to plain text and ANSI codes.

    Args:
        ansi_text (str): A String containing ANSI codes.

    Yields:
        AnsiToken: A named tuple of (plain, sgr, osc)
    """

    position = 0
    sgr: Optional[str]
    osc: Optional[str]
    for match in re_ansi.finditer(ansi_text):
        start, end = match.span(0)
        osc, sgr = match.groups()
        if start > position:
            yield _AnsiToken(ansi_text[position:start])

                yield _AnsiToken("", sgr[1:-1], osc)

from rich.ansi import AnsiDecoder
from rich.console import Console
from rich.style import Style
from rich.text import Span, Text


def test_decode():
    console = Console(
        force_terminal=True, legacy_windows=False, color_system="truecolor"
    )
    console.begin_capture()
    console.print("Hello")
    console.print("[b]foo[/b]")
    console.print("[link http://example.org]bar")
    console.print("[#ff0000 on color(200)]red")
    console.print("[color(200) on #ff0000]red")
    terminal_codes = console.end_capture()

    decoder = AnsiDecoder()
    lines = list(decoder.decode(terminal_codes))

    expected = [
        Text("Hello"),
        Text("foo", spans=[Span(0, 3, Style.parse("bold"))]),
        Text("bar", spans=[Span(0, 3, Style.parse("link http://example.org"))]),
        Text("red", spans=[Span(0, 3, Style.parse("#ff0000 on color(200)"))]),
        Text("red", spans=[Span(0, 3, Style.parse("color(200) on #ff0000"))]),
    ]

    assert lines == expected

FILES: rich/ansi.py:13-14
ROOT CAUSE: The ANSI regex `re_ansi` matches escape sequences starting with `\x1b` followed by a range of characters that includes private escape sequences (`\x1b0`-`\x1b?`). These should be stripped/ignored to prevent cursor jumping and garbage output.
CHANGE: Update the regex `re_ansi` to exclude the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` range. Specifically, change `[@-Z\\-_]` to `[@-Z\\-_]` (it already is, but the issue is the other part) and ensure the first part of the OR condition for SGR/CSI sequences doesn't capture these. Actually, the problem is that `\x1b[0-?]` sequences are being passed through. The regex `(?:\\x1b([(@-Z\\\\-_]|\\\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))` captures single-character sequences in `[@-Z\\-_]`. To strip `\x1b0` through `\x1b?`, we should ensure they are not matched by the regex so they are treated as plain text and subsequently filtered, or better, modify the regex to match them but the tokenizer to discard them. 

Wait, looking at `_ansi_tokenize`:
```python
        if sgr:
            if sgr == "(":
                position = end + 1
                continue
            if sgr.endswith("m"):
                yield _AnsiToken("", sgr[1:-1], osc)
        else:
            yield _AnsiToken("", sgr, osc)
```
If the regex matches `\x1b0`, `sgr` will be `0`. It will yield `_AnsiToken("", "0", None)`.

To fix this, we can change the regex `[@-Z\\-_]` to start from `@` (which is `\x40`), skipping `0-?` (which are `\x30-\x3f`). 
The current range `[@-Z\\-_]` is `\x40` to `\x5a`, `\x5c`, `\x5f`, `\x5f`.
Wait, `\x1b0` is NOT matched by `[@-Z\\-_]`.
Wait, `\x1b0` is matched by `\x1b([(@-Z\\-_]|...)`. 
`0` is NOT in `[@-Z\\-_]`.
Wait, `\x1b0` is not matched at all by the current regex? 
Let's check the regex again: `(?:\\x1b([(@-Z\\\\-_]|\\\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))`
`(` is `\x28`. `0` is `\x30`. 
So `\x1b(` matches. `\x1b0` does NOT match.

If `\x1b0` does not match the regex, it is treated as plain text:
`if start > position: yield _AnsiToken(ansi_text[position:start])`
So `\x1b0` is yielded as plain text.
To strip it, it MUST be matched by the regex but then ignored by the tokenizer.

The requested change is to "update the ANSI parser to ignore the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` escape sequences".
This means updating the regex to include them: `[@-Z\\-_]` -> `[0-?@-Z\\-_]`.
And then the tokenizer will yield `_AnsiToken("", sgr, osc)` where `sgr` is `0`-`?`. 
Wait, if it yields it, it might still be printed. 
The tokenizer should be updated to NOT yield them.

Actually, the simplest way is to add `[0-?]` to the regex and then in `_ansi_tokenize`, filter them out.

TEST: tests/test_ansi.py (add a test case for `\x1b0` through `\x1b?`)

                continue

            yield _AnsiToken("", sgr, osc)
